title: Desk Memo: Flood Map Revisions and Elevation Certificates on FloodGuard Policies
content:
The FloodGuard Private Flood Policy records a flood map revision or a new elevation certificate when the named insured or the lender provides the revised map panel or the certificate. The zone, the map revision date and the elevation certificate result on file are then updated.

**Premium effect.** A zone or elevation change never changes the premium of the current term; it is rated at the next renewal offer.

**Map revision window.** A revision that moves the building into zone A, AE or VE opens the map revision window for a new purchase at that address.

**Revision out of a high-risk zone.** A revision that moves the building out of zone A, AE or VE is a reason the lender may drop its requirement, but it is never an accepted cancellation reason.

| What is provided | Who may provide it | What changes now | What waits |
|---|---|---|---|
| A revised map panel | The named insured or the lender | The zone and map revision date on file | Rating of the change, until the next renewal offer |
| A new elevation certificate | The named insured or the lender | The elevation certificate result on file | Rating of the change, until the next renewal offer |

**Hypothetical cases.**

- A building moves from zone X to zone AE by a revision in the middle of a term. The current term's premium is unchanged; the new zone is rated at the next renewal offer, and a new purchase at that address may fall within the map revision window.
- A building moves from zone AE to zone X. The lender may drop its flood requirement, but a request to cancel the FloodGuard policy midterm on that ground is not an accepted cancellation reason.
